subject: Making a non-reactive UI for model fitting

messages.author: 98166cebe3eff2a1
messages.subject: Making a non-reactive UI for model fitting
parts:
I've (or a colleague of mine has) mocked up a simple UI in Shiny for fitting a regression model. There is a dropdown list where you the user selects one or more predictor variables, and the browser then displays some output from the resulting model.

At the moment, the UI is reactive, meaning that the model is dynamically refitted for every variable that is added and removed. This works fine for a small dataset, but when dealing with a large number of rows and columns, it becomes a bit tedious. How would I change the UI so that instead of updating the model each time a variable is selected or deselected, the user can choose a subset of variables and then press a "Calculate" button to do the fit?

Here is the code:

ui.R:


ui <- fluidPage(
 
  # Application title
  titlePanel("Prototype Shiny for Generic Data"),
 
  # Sidebar with selections for data/plot control
  sidebarLayout(
    sidebarPanel(
      selectInput( inputId='Exclusions', label='exc', choices=CHOICES, selected=NULL, multiple=TRUE )
          ), # End sidebarPanel
   
    # Show the selected plot
    tabsetPanel(
        tabPanel( 'Time Series', plotOutput( 'timePlot' ), value='time' )
      , tabPanel( 'Data', tableOutput( 'mainTable' ), value='data' )
      , id='plotPanels')
  ) # End sidebarLayout
)# End fluidPage


server.R:

shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {
  
    # MYDATA and CHOICES defined in global.R
    ## Computation
    getRegression <- function()
    {
        regVars <- setdiff(CHOICES, input$Exclusions)
        regVars <- if(length(regVars) == 0) "1" else paste(regVars, collapse="+")
        fm <- as.formula(paste("DFlag ~", regVars), globalenv())

        modelCall <- substitute(glm(.fm, data=MYDATA, family=binomial), list(.fm=fm))
        eval(modelCall, globalenv())
    }
    getNewPD <- function()
    {
        model <- getRegression()
        predPD <- predict(model, MYDATA, type="response")
        cbind(MYDATA, predPD)
    }
 
    getTimeData <- function(){

        predDf <- getNewPD()
        timeData1 <- predDf %>%
            group_by(Date) %>%
            summarise(Exposure=sum(Exposure),
                      ODR=mean(DFlag),
                      oldPD=mean(PD),
                      newPD=mean(predPD))
        timeData1$Date <- as.Date(timeData1$Date)
        timeData1
    }

    output$timePlot <- renderPlot({
        timeData <- getTimeData()
        p <- ggplot(timeData, aes(x=Date, y=Default, colour=Type)) +
            geom_line(aes(y=ODR, colour="ODR")) +
            geom_line(aes(y=oldPD, colour="oldPD")) +
            geom_line(aes(y=newPD, colour="newPD"))
        p
    })
 
    output$mainTable <- renderTable( head(MYDATA),  digits=2 )
 
}) # End shinyServer


(Yes, the dropdown list actually selects variables to remove from the model. It's one of the quirks of this project.)

messages.subject: Re: Making a non-reactive UI for model fitting
parts:
Yes, as per Huidong Tian's suggestion, use an actionButton for "Calculate".  But first read up on isolating:  http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/isolation.html.  Then you can do this sort of thing:

output$yourresult <- renderWhatever({
  input$calculate  # for dependency on the action button with id "calculate"
  [code to make your output, with isolate(input$whateverinput) for all required inputs]
})
